sounds.prompt: A steel handcuff ratchet closing around a wrist: a quick metallic ratcheting zip of a few teeth and a final sharp locking click. Real nickel-plated police handcuffs, 1980s, a few small steel parts, nothing else. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no music, no voice, no chain rattle.
sounds.reason: Takes 2 and 3 are short and clean: 0.24 s of five even ratchet teeth and 0.21 s of a ratchet burst, a clack and a final lock click, each ending on its last click with no tail. Take 1 has a half-second gap in the middle that reads as two actions, take 4 is a slow fade of ten teeth (0.67 s) that outlasts the 0.5 s the strands take to swing shut. Two takes for variety between cuffings.

sounds.prompt: A single small steel click of a handcuff key releasing the lock and the swinging arm of a steel handcuff springing open, one short metallic snick. Recorded close, dry, no reverb, no music, no voice, no chain rattle.
sounds.reason: Take 2 is one 90 ms spring snick with a small click after it, the strands springing out when the lock lets go. Take 1 is a string of faint ticks before the click, take 3 is 50 ms, too short to read as a swing.
